title: Notices and warnings
subtitle: OUT OF ORDER, KEEP OFF THE GRASS, MIND THE STEP
summary: Understand the short English notices and warnings you see on doors, machines and signs in public places.

lesson.heading: Notices: information
rows: on a machine, e.g. a vending machine
in the window of a hotel
all the tickets have been sold
you can go in without paying
lesson.note: A **vending machine** is a machine that sells drinks and snacks.

lesson.heading: Do this!
lesson.text: Some notices tell you what to do. **PLEASE QUEUE OTHER SIDE** in a bank or post office means: wait in a line on the other side of this notice. **KEEP RIGHT** (or **KEEP LEFT**) means: stay on the right side, for example on the underground.

examples.text: **PLEASE QUEUE OTHER SIDE** - wait in a line on the other side of this sign.
**KEEP RIGHT** - stay on the right side as you walk.
**KEEP OFF THE GRASS** - do not walk on the grass.
**SILENCE - EXAMINATION IN PROGRESS** - be quiet, an exam is happening now.

lesson.heading: Don't do this!
lesson.text: Other notices tell you what you must not do. Most of them begin with **NO** or **DO NOT**.

examples.text: **NO PARKING** - you cannot leave your car here.
**NO ENTRY** - you cannot go in here.
**NO EXIT** - you cannot go out here.
**PLEASE DO NOT DISTURB** - on a hotel door: leave me to sleep.

lesson.heading: More 'do not' notices
rows: an airport or station waiting area
don't put a bag down and walk away
DO NOT LEAN OUT OF THE WINDOW
keep your head and arms inside
PLEASE DO NOT FEED THE ANIMALS
do not give food to the animals
do not leave your car here

lesson.heading: Warnings
lesson.text: A **warning** tells you that something bad may happen. Many warnings start with **MIND** (= be careful about) or **FRAGILE**.

examples.text: **MIND YOUR HEAD** - take care you don't hit your head on a low door.
**MIND THE STEP** - be careful, there's a step.
**FRAGILE** - on a parcel: be careful, this will break easily.

lesson.heading: Other notices you may see
rows: people on bicycles must get off their bikes
there is no way out for cars at the other end

lesson.text: **Mind** in a notice means *be careful about*: MIND THE STEP, MIND YOUR HEAD, MIND THE GAP.

exercises.prompt: Complete the warning on a low doorway: MIND YOUR ___ .
exercises.explanation: MIND YOUR HEAD warns you not to hit your head on a low door.

exercises.prompt: Complete the warning at the bottom of a doorway: MIND THE ___ .
exercises.explanation: MIND THE STEP means be careful, there is a step.
ADMISSION FREE means you can go in without paying.

exercises.prompt: Complete the notice on a broken vending machine: OUT OF ___ .
exercises.explanation: OUT OF ORDER means the machine is not working.

exercises.prompt: Complete the park notice: KEEP OFF THE ___ .
exercises.explanation: KEEP OFF THE GRASS means do not walk on the grass.

exercises.prompt: Complete the notice outside an exam room: SILENCE - EXAMINATION IN ___ .
exercises.explanation: EXAMINATION IN PROGRESS means an exam is happening now.

exercises.prompt: A hotel window says NO VACANCIES. What does it mean?
options: The hotel is closed for repairs.
exercises.explanation: NO VACANCIES means there are no free rooms - the hotel is full.

exercises.prompt: You see SOLD OUT outside a theatre. What does it mean?
options: All the tickets have been sold.
The theatre has been sold to a new owner.
The show has finished for ever.
exercises.explanation: SOLD OUT means all the tickets have been sold.

exercises.prompt: A parcel says FRAGILE. What should you do?
options: Be careful - it will break easily.
exercises.explanation: FRAGILE warns you that the contents break easily.

exercises.prompt: Where would you see each notice?

pairs.right: in a bank or post office

pairs.left: PLEASE DO NOT FEED THE ANIMALS

exercises.prompt: Match each place with the notice you could see there.

pairs.left: in a busy airport waiting area
on a hotel room door at 9 am
above the window of a train
pairs.right: DO NOT LEAN OUT OF THE WINDOW

exercises.prompt: Does the notice tell you to do something, or not to do something?

exercises.statement: NO EXIT on a door means you cannot go out through that door.
exercises.explanation: Correct. NO EXIT means you cannot go out here; NO ENTRY means you cannot go in.

exercises.statement: CYCLISTS DISMOUNT HERE means cyclists can ride faster from this point.
exercises.explanation: False. It means people on bicycles must get off their bikes here.

exercises.prompt: Put the words in order to make the notice you see in a zoo.
exercises.answer: Please do not feed the animals
exercises.explanation: Feed = give food to. The notice asks visitors not to give food to the animals.

exercises.prompt: Put the words in order to make the notice you see above a train window.
exercises.answer: Do not lean out of the window
exercises.explanation: Lean out = put your head or body through the open window.
